concerns.text: Task T005 implements dynamic selection from OpenML but fails to satisfy FR-001 and Constitution Principle VII which mandate datasets from 'UCI/OpenML' covering 'feature dimensions'. The task logic only sorts by sample size (N) and ignores the 'feature dimensions' constraint, risking a dataset set that satisfies N-diversity but fails feature-diversity. This is a silent relaxation of the constitutional requirement.

Spec FR-004 and SC-002 explicitly require computing Pearson correlation between 'Coefficient of Variation (CV)' and dataset properties. Task T019a computes correlation on 'CV vs log(N)' (mixing raw CV with log-transformed N), while T019b computes 'log(CV) vs log(N)'. Neither task implements the spec's primary requirement of 'CV vs [properties]' (implied raw vs raw or consistent transformation). The Plan's rejection of raw correlation as 'tautological' contradicts the Spec's explicit FR-004, and the tasks follow the Plan, effectively weakening the Spec's requirement without a formal amendment.

Spec FR-007 requires multiple-comparison correction for 'the set of hypothesis tests'. Task T026 pools p-values from two distinct statistical families (Correlation tests T019a/b and Permutation tests T025) into a single Holm-Bonferroni correction. The Spec does not authorize pooling these distinct families (correlation vs. variance difference). This risks over-correction (inflating Type II error) for the correlation analysis, violating the intent of FR-007 to control FWER for the specific tests described in SC-002 and SC-003 separately or with explicit justification.

Constitution Principle VII requires datasets to span 'feature dimensions'. Task T005's selection logic (Step 4) only sorts by 'n_samples' and takes top 5 from size bins. It contains no logic to ensure diversity in 'n_features'. This is a silent relaxation of the constitutional constraint regarding feature dimension diversity.
